messages:
Aisha: Heads-up — saw a regression on long-chat tests after yesterday's kernel routing change. Intermittent OOMs during early KV-cache warmup. Stacktrace points to big allocator churn.
Ravi: Can you paste the exact OOM log? is it from CUDA or our slab allocator? :thinking:
Aisha: CUDA OOM message but our allocator trace shows a lot of small frees/allocs around the same time. snippet:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 256.00 MiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total, 29.20 GiB free)
[allocator] allocate(size=268435456) -> fail
[alloc-trace] split_size=64MB expandable_segments=true gc_threshold=0.7
```
Jon: That gc_threshold line is our debug print — looks like garbage_collection_threshold currently 0.7. Did we change max_split_size_mb recently?
Taylor: Yes, yesterday I bumped max_split_size_mb from 32 to 128 to reduce split churn for short sequences. Might be interacting badly with expandable_segments enabled.
Sofia: If max_split_size_mb is large we avoid splitting big free blocks which increases fragmentation for lots of small allocations (kv cache frames). expandable_segments makes the allocator grow segment count instead of splitting — could exacerbate.
Ravi: Proposed quick repro: run long-chat perf test with three configs: (A) expandable_segments=true, max_split_size_mb=128, gc=0.7 (B) expandable_segments=false, max_split_size_mb=32, gc=0.7 (C) expandable_segments=true, max_split_size_mb=32, gc=0.5. Measure peak and OOMs.
Aisha: I ran A and C on a dev box. A -> OOM around 1200th token during warmup. C -> no OOM, slightly higher steady fragmentation but survived. Numbers:
- A: peak resident 28.9 GiB, OOM
- C: peak resident 27.1 GiB, no OOM, 0.8% perf regression in latency but stable
Jon: Sounds like lowering max_split_size_mb helps. GC threshold drop to 0.5 also reduces live retention by forcing earlier reclamation.
Taylor: Could we try a hybrid: keep expandable_segments but detect warmup phase and temporarily set max_split_size_mb=32 and gc=0.6? We can toggle at request-level until kv-warmup finishes.
Sofia: Implementation idea: when route==chat and seq_len_growth_rate>threshold, set allocator hints: {expandable_segments: true, max_split_size_mb: 32, garbage_collection_threshold: 0.6}. Emit metric flag so we can roll back.
Ravi: Agree to try config toggle. Also add a perf counter for "small_alloc_chain" to see fragmentation pattern. Add quick nvprof-like allocation timeline to CI.
Aisha: I'll push a canary patch that switches knobs during first N tokens of a session (N=64). If stable for 24h we'll promote.
ci-bot: deploy/canary started by Aisha — env=canary-alloc-tweaks, sha=3b7c9d2
Jon: One more: let's not forget to test with batching/autobatch enabled. Batching changes allocation simultaneity and can amplify the issue.
Sofia: Good point — I saw the OOMs more on batched runs. Maybe batching + large max_split_size_mb causes many threads to hold big chunks.
Taylor: For the patch, keep god-level logging toggled behind feature-flag so we can turn it on if we get another OOM and grab allocator histogram.
Aisha: I'll open a follow-up ticket with the experiment results and include the memory graphs, nvprof snippets, and exact knob deltas. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Ravi: @Aisha please capture a pprof-style flamechart for allocations too. That helped last time.
Aisha: Will do. If canary is green after 6h I'll post results here.
ci-bot: deploy/canary finished — status=success, duration=4m12s
Jon: Nice. If canary looks good we should add a short-term auto-toggle: when warmup_alloc_rate > X -> apply narrower split and slightly lower gc.
Sofia: Opening a small RFC for a warmup-aware allocator profile. cc: @Taylor @Ravi
Aisha: RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/alloc-warmup-profile — contains command outputs and experiment notes.
